headline: City Resident Sues Local Politician For 'Encroaching On Personal Traffic Delay' During Unauthorized Rally
body:
Local resident Suman Chatterjee has filed a formal grievance against the state’s ruling party leadership, alleging that their decision to hold an unpermitted students' wing rally effectively 'usurped and monopolized' his legally designated time for sitting in gridlocked traffic. Chatterjee, a professional data analyst who counts on his daily 90-minute commute to contemplate the existential void, claims the rally’s sudden arrival cleared the road entirely, leaving him at his desk before he had reached a proper state of road-rage induced enlightenment.

'I had a very specific playlist prepared for that exact stretch of the flyover,' said Chatterjee, while clutching a stack of printed Google Maps logs as evidence of his lost stationary time. 'When the rally caused the police to divert everyone away from the usual bottleneck, I arrived at the office thirty minutes early. I wasn't mentally prepared for a productive morning, and frankly, I feel robbed of the quiet, exhaust-filled introspection I paid for with my fuel taxes.'

Legal experts are baffled by the claim, noting that while the rally itself may have technically violated high court orders, the act of speeding up a commute is usually considered a public service. 'Mr. Chatterjee is essentially arguing for his right to be inconvenienced,' said civil lawyer Aniruddha Das. 'He contends that by clearing the traffic, the political organizers have committed a form of anti-bureaucratic interference that disrupts the established natural rhythm of the city’s rush hour.'

As the case moves toward a potential hearing, officials are bracing for a wave of counter-suits from commuters who feel that any rally, authorized or otherwise, should be required to provide a mandatory minimum of four hours of stationary road time. For now, Chatterjee remains optimistic that the judiciary will uphold his right to remain stuck behind a bus for the duration of his contractual morning commute.
caption: Local man really just wanted his 90 minutes of silence in traffic and we respect the commitment. #Kolkata #TrafficDiaries #Priorities #OfficeLife (satire)
